final_answer:
>>> The classic "trolley problem" is a long-standing ethical thought experiment, and there’s no universally agreed-upon answer. If you pull the lever, you intentionally kill one person to save five. If you do nothing, you allow five people to die. Many ethical frameworks (e.g., utilitarianism) would argue pulling the lever is preferable because it minimizes overall harm. Others (e.g., deontological ethics) focus on the morality of the action itself, sometimes opposing the deliberate taking of a life even to save others.  

>>> If the one person is your child, the decision becomes deeply personal and emotionally charged. The calculus of "greater good" may feel less straightforward when the sacrifice involves a loved one. Some might still argue the principle remains the same (minimize deaths), while others might feel the relationship changes the moral weight. Ultimately, the answer often depends on your ethical stance and how you weigh intent, relationships, and consequences.
